title: Broadcom Lends Anthropic $42B to Offset AI Funding Shortage

tickers.name: SK hynix Inc. American Depositary Shares

summary:
Hock Tan believes that the availability of cash will soon be the primary constraint on the development of advanced neural networks. While speaking at an event in Singapore, the Broadcom chief executive stated that access to capital, rather than chip or memory shortages, could become the industry's main growth bottleneck. Broadcom is already attempting to mitigate these constraints by backing a debt package of up to $42 billion for Anthropic to fund the leasing of AI semiconductors, even as Tan cautioned that many current investors are betting like they are in a casino.

The remarks contributed to a global chip stock sell-off, with Samsung falling as much as 8.8%, SK Hynix sliding 9.2%, and Micron dropping 4%. Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan agreed that capital costs are a front-line challenge, though he noted that hardware will remain in short supply for the next 2 to 3 years. Despite the funding risks, Broadcom projects its AI chip revenue will double to $230 billion by 2028, while ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt noted that the U.S. capital markets are uniquely equipped to handle the trillion-dollar costs of the AI buildout.

selectedTweets.text:
🦔Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said Monday that a lot of AI investors have no clue what they’re investing in and act like they’re in a casino. He also compared companies spending on AI to a kid who burns through $10 of arcade tokens in 10 minutes and learns nothing.

My Take
He’s not wrong, but it’s a strange thing to hear from the guy running the house. Broadcom agreed to lend Anthropic up to $42 billion to lease its chips, and Tan still projects his AI chip revenue doubling to $230 billion in 2028. A lot of the money he’s calling casino money ends up as Broadcom revenue.

If businesses keep burning through AI spending like that kid with the arcade tokens, those budgets get cut, and the chip orders behind them shrink too. Tan also warned that AI companies could start running short of money to borrow, and Firmus already pulled its IPO last week when investors balked at the price. If companies cut their AI budgets or the money dries up, I have a hard time seeing Broadcom hit $230 billion in AI chip sales by 2028.

Hedgie🤗

Ex Google CEO, Dr. Eric Schmidt: AI may hit a money wall before it hits a power wall.

Perf per watt had a good run. At 6%, a trillion in debt costs $60B a year.

"The real limit to AI is not energy; it is actually cash. When you add up the cost of these things, if you take round numbers, say $50 bn per gigawatt, then 10 gigawatts is half a trillion dollars.

How many companies, countries, and so forth can hand an industry a trillion dollars of capital? Very, very few. The Chinese could certainly do it. I do not know if they are doing it, but I am going to try to find out.

In America, there are people who hope that is going to happen. It is interesting that you can finance these things because the brilliance of the American capital market allows us to borrow that kind of money. For example, the Europeans cannot do this, which they are sort of sore about."
